title: The box that holds valuables
summary: R.E.P.O. has a box you put valuables into rather than only carry them: it checks what is inside it, holds them up to a value limit, answers on a moving text screen when it will not take something, absorbs what fits, and then sends it all upward and away.
body: One of the objects in the game is a box that takes valuables rather than a crate that simply holds them. It has a state of its own and a part that looks at what is inside it, which is why it can answer you instead of only being a container.

It is limited by worth as well as by space. The box carries a value limit, so a small object can be turned away while a large one is accepted, and what fits is a question about value rather than only about size.
It opens and closes on curves. Both actions have a curve and a length of their own, with a sound for each, so the lid moves rather than snapping between two positions.
There is a point inside for what you put in. The box knows where that is, which is what lets the rest of the object work on a valuable the moment it is dropped in.

It answers on a screen. The box has a text screen with a part that animates it, and the screen moves through a starting, a middle and an ending position and rotation, so a message arrives rather than simply appearing.

The answer is specific. There are separate messages for something being too big, for the box being too full and for the extraction itself, along with separate sounds for an error, a success and a neutral message, which is why a refusal is readable rather than silent.
It absorbs what it takes. There is a duration for the absorb and a sound for it, and the box has a shortest time it will stay open, so a quick drop cannot be followed by an instant close.

It gives everything back at the end. There is a duration for the extraction, a prefab for what comes out, an upward speed and a rotation speed, and a maximum distance it will travel, which is why a filled box performs its own finish rather than waiting to be picked up.
It breaks apart as well. The box has particles for breaking, so it can also end as bits rather than only as a container that opens.
What this entry does not tell you: what the value limit is, how many valuables fit, or how long an extraction takes. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The box has a state of its own and a part that checks what is inside it.
The box carries a value limit.
It opens and closes with its own curves, a duration and a sound for each.
facts.evidence: identifiers: animationCurveOpen, animationCurveClose, animationDuration, soundOpen, soundClose

facts.claim: There is a point inside the box where valuables are placed.
It answers on a text screen with an animator, moving through a starting, a middle and an ending position and rotation.
facts.evidence: identifiers: textScreen, textScreenAnimatorTransform, textScreenStartPosition, textScreenStartRotation, textScreenMidPosition, textScreenMidRotation, textScreenEndPosition, textScreenEndRotation

facts.claim: There are separate messages for something too big, for the box being too full and for extraction, with separate error, success and neutral sounds.
facts.evidence: identifiers: localizedMessageTooBig, localizedMessageTooFull, localizedMessageExtract, soundMessageError, soundMessageSuccess, soundMessageNeutral

facts.claim: It absorbs what it takes, with a duration for the absorb and a sound, and it has a shortest time it stays open.
Extraction has its own duration, a prefab for what comes out, an upward speed, a rotation speed and a maximum distance.
facts.evidence: identifiers: extractionDuration, valuableExtractingPrefab, extractUpwardSpeed, extractRotationSpeed, extractMaxDistance

facts.claim: The box has particles for breaking.

alt.en: Diagram: a valuable is dropped into the box, the box checks it against its value limit, answers on its screen, absorbs it, and sends everything upward at the end.
alt.zh: 示意图：把珍贵物放进箱子、箱子按价值上限检查、在屏幕上给出答复、将其吸收，最后把所有东西向上送出。
